screening_decisions.reason: The article describes a mathematical modelling study, not a primary diagnostic accuracy investigation of a point‑of‑care test in a prospective cohort of non‑pregnant women/men.
This work is a meta‑epidemiological analysis of publication bias, not an original diagnostic accuracy study of chlamydia in the target population.

Prospective trial comparing several index tests (DFA, OIA, culture, PCR) with a PCR reference standard in a large urban STD clinic; participants are women of reproductive age, and 2 × 2 data are reported.

Pilot diagnostic accuracy study of the QuickVue rapid test versus PCR in endocervical specimens from women (both high‑ and low‑prevalence groups); all participants received index and reference tests and 2 × 2 tables are presented.
Guideline document; no primary diagnostic accuracy data on a point‑of‑care chlamydia test.
Narrative review discussing the state of rapid STI tests; does not present original diagnostic accuracy results.
Prospective field evaluation of two rapid POC tests against NAAT reference standard in men and women of reproductive age; reports sensitivity, specificity and 2 × 2 data.
Large prospective diagnostic accuracy study of a rapid test versus Roche NAAT in non‑pregnant women of reproductive age; full 2 × 2 data provided.
Prospective cohort evaluating a rapid urine test against PCR in men; all participants received both index and reference tests and 2 × 2 results are reported.
Policy/recommendation paper; no primary diagnostic accuracy data.
Systematic review, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Evidence summary for guidelines; no original diagnostic accuracy investigation.

The article is a systematic review summarising existing evidence rather than a primary diagnostic accuracy study. According to the selection criteria, only primary prospective diagnostic accuracy studies are eligible.
This is another systematic review of nucleic acid amplification tests, not an original diagnostic accuracy investigation. The protocol excludes reviews and case‑control designs.

The study directly evaluates the performance of a rapid point‑of‑care optical immunoassay against culture, DFA and PCR, providing 2×2 data. It enrols women at an STD clinic (presumably non‑pregnant, reproductive‑age) and reports sensitivity and specificity, matching the inclusion criteria.
This is a prevalence survey, not a diagnostic accuracy study, and does not present index test vs reference standard data.

A cross‑sectional diagnostic accuracy study evaluating several rapid tests (including a Chlamydia rapid test) against nucleic acid amplification methods in symptomatic women, with sensitivity and specificity reported. Meets all inclusion criteria.

Primary comparative diagnostic accuracy study of multiple index tests versus amplified reference standards, with 2×2 data derived from a large cohort of women. Fits the protocol’s population and design requirements.

Focuses on a point‑of‑care optical immunoassay in adolescent females, reports sensitivity and specificity against two NAATs, and provides 2×2 data. Population (adolescent, non‑pregnant) matches inclusion criteria.

A pilot diagnostic accuracy study assessing a rapid test against PCR in asymptomatic men, with reported sensitivity and specificity. Aligns with inclusion criteria (asymptomatic, non‑pregnant men, primary care setting).
The paper reports prevalence data using PCR only; it does not evaluate a point‑of‑care index test against a reference standard, thus does not meet diagnostic accuracy study criteria.
A narrative review of laboratory methods rather than a primary diagnostic accuracy investigation.
Surveillance study reporting prevalence of multiple STIs; no index test performance data.
Observational prevalence study; does not assess a rapid point‑of‑care test versus a reference standard.
Primary diagnostic accuracy evaluation of a rapid POC test against PCR in a high‑risk population (sex workers). Provides sensitivity, specificity and 2×2 data, satisfying inclusion criteria.
A review article summarising available tests; no original diagnostic accuracy data.
Prospective performance evaluation of a new rapid test with self‑collected vaginal swabs, reporting sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV against PCR and SDA assays. Meets all selection criteria.
Focuses on serovar distribution and clinical correlation; does not evaluate diagnostic accuracy of a rapid test.
Prospective diagnostic accuracy study of a manufacturer’s CRT compared to NAAT in women, with detailed sensitivity and specificity data. Aligns with inclusion criteria.

Methodological paper about literature searching; does not present primary diagnostic accuracy data.
Cross‑sectional diagnostic accuracy study comparing a rapid optical immunoassay to ligase chain reaction, reporting sensitivity and specificity. Fits inclusion criteria.
Evaluates three POC tests against NAAT in women, provides sensitivity, specificity, and 2×2 data. Meets population (non‑pregnant women), prospective design, and reporting requirements.
Literature review of risk factors; no primary diagnostic accuracy evaluation.

Prototype evaluation of a new POC test with sensitivity and specificity data (initial low, later improved). Provides 2×2 data and follows a prospective evaluation framework, matching inclusion criteria.
